newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian industry posted negative growth in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Colombian industry posted negative growth in 1996.

text.p: Colombian industry slumped into negative growth of -0.7 percent in 1996, a sharp reversal of 3.4 percent growth in 1995, according to a business survey issued Tuesday.

The closely-watched survey, produced by the National Association of Industrialists and based on responses from business leaders across Colombia, said industrial sales last year suffered negative growth of -1.0 percent, down from a bubbling 3.6 percent rate of growth in 1995.

Twenty-one of 28 different industrial sectors participating in the survey reported cuts in production last year. The only growth was in oil-related activities, according to the industrial group known as ANDI.

Participants in the survey cited last year's political scandal and uncertainty stemming from charges that President Ernesto Samper financed his 1994 election campaign with drug money as among leading reasons for the economic downturn.
They also blamed the country's booming trade in contraband goods and said high domestic interest rates had seriously eroded demand. ((-- Juan Guillermo Londono, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
